references.text: The same command to destroy the instruments of idolatry—altars, pillars, and carved images—when the Israelites enter the land.
Command to destroy all the places where the nations worshiped their gods, including the high places, and to break down their sacred pillars and images.
Prohibition against worshiping the Canaanite gods and command to tear down their sacred pillars.
Command to tear down the Canaanites' altars, smash their sacred pillars, and cut down their Asherah poles.
Reiteration of the command to drive out the inhabitants and destroy their idolatry.
Joshua drove out the inhabitants and their kings from the land, fulfilling the command in Numbers.
Warning against making a covenant with the people of the land and command to tear down their altars—Israel did not obey.
Warning of judgment if Israel builds high places and sacred pillars like the Canaanite peoples.
King Hezekiah removed the high places, smashed the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asherah pole—in line with this command.
